recipes.name: Squash Dressing
ingredients_raw: 2.5 pounds yellow squash, cut into chunks
2 (10.5 ounce) cans cream of chicken soup
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 (1 pound) package Mexican-style processed cheese food (such as Mexican Velveeta®), cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 15x17-inch baking dish.
Place squash in a medium saucepan with about 1 cup water; cover and cook over medium-low heat until soft, about 15 minutes. Drain, saving about 3/4 cup cooking liquid; set aside.
Break cornbread into small chunks, transfer to a medium bowl, and chop with a table knife until crumbled. Set aside.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add celery, onion, and bell pepper; cook and stir until soft, about 10 minutes. Combine condensed soups and eggs in a large bowl; stir in celery mixture and season with salt and black pepper.

Stir cornbread into soup mixture. Gently stir in cooked squash. Add enough reserved cooking liquid until dressing reaches consistency of cooked oatmeal (slightly soupy). Stir in cheese; transfer dressing to the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until set and lightly browned, about 1 hour. Let stand for 10 to 15 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This Southern-style squash dressing recipe, made with yellow squash, is similar to cornbread dressing. Savory and comforting, it’s perfect for holidays.

review.reviewBody: My mom started making this recipe in the early '90's. It is really good. However, save yourself some trouble and use shredded cheese. Using real cheese bumps it up to 5 stars. Also, you won't need the extra liquid. Extra liquid keeps it from "setting up" and makes it too loose to be like stuffing/dressing.
love this stuffing. very tasty and wonderful.
